panels.title: Offered Load: k6 Request Rate by Scenario
panels.description: loadgen (RFC-0001 D4, ADR-0006): k6's own request rate, pushed via -o experimental-prometheus-rw. Compare against Observed Latency to the right -- offered load next to what the system actually delivered.

panels.title: Observed Latency: Backend p95 by Endpoint
panels.description: Whitebox RED p95 (services/backend), same expression as the main DevOps Demo dashboard -- what the backend actually served under loadgen's offered load.

panels.title: k6 Worst Tagged-Series p95 by Scenario
panels.description: Worst tagged-series p95 within each scenario: k6's remote-write output emits one p95 series per tag combination, so max() by scenario reports the slowest tag combo, not a combined scenario-wide p95. k6's own http_req_duration Trend, mapped to k6_http_req_duration_p95 by the Prometheus remote-write output (K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS=p(95),p(99),avg, loadgen/README.md). Client-side view: includes DNS/connect/TLS that the backend's own RED metric (left) does not.

panels.title: Error Rate by Scenario (unexpected responses)
panels.description: Fraction of k6_http_reqs_total tagged expected_response=false -- a proper request-volume-weighted rate() over the Counter, not k6_http_req_failed_rate's own Rate-sink snapshots (those are one value per unique tag combination per push interval; naively averaging them across combinations is not weighted by how many requests each combination represents and reads noisy/wrong in practice, verified live in this PR's e2e run). abuse's intentional 4xx/422 are marked expected via http.expectedStatuses() in loadgen/scenarios/main.js, so they carry expected_response=true and do not inflate this series.

panels.title: gRPC p95 Duration (grpc scenario)
panels.description: Unary ListItems/GetItemStats against api:50051 (RFC-0001 D3). grpc has no http_req_failed equivalent -- loadgen_grpc_call_failed (bottom right) is this scenario's correctness signal instead.

panels.title: Active VUs
panels.description: k6_vus: total virtual users currently executing across every scenario (global gauge, not tagged per-scenario).

panels.title: Abuse / gRPC Correctness
panels.description: loadgen's own custom Rate metrics (loadgen/scenarios/main.js): did the abuse scenario's responses match the status it was designed to provoke, and did gRPC unary calls return grpc.StatusOK. Both should sit at (or very near) 0.
